question: Should the current repair-mutation guard stack be marked ready and landed once the failing `pnpm check` is resolved, or should it remain staged for additional production-rollout validation?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but it changes the final authorization boundary for automated merges, closes, comments, labels, receipts, and deferred state publication; choosing the rollout threshold requires ownership of operational fail-closed behavior.

options.title: Resolve check and land
options.body: Inspect and clear the current required-check failure, refresh exact-head review, and merge the complete guard stack as the intended continuation of the merged precursor.

options.title: Stage additional rollout proof
options.body: Keep the PR draft while exercising representative apply, post-flight, closeout, and expired-credential paths in a controlled workflow run before marking it ready.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Leave the draft open without landing if maintainers are not prepared to adopt the stricter fail-closed mutation boundary and its operational recovery requirements.

recommendation.title: Resolve check and land
recommendation.body: Inspect and clear the current required-check failure, refresh exact-head review, and merge the complete guard stack as the intended continuation of the merged precursor.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the merged precursor and the current implementation history across the affected repair mutation paths.
